main_body: Stone-tiled roof (rows 0-16) on two wooden posts, with a gray basin holding a blue water panel at rows 30-42
top_band: Light gray ridge cap at rows 1-3, then blue-gray tile slope rows 4-15 that reads as the roof's top surface; the dark underside edge sits at rows 16-17
evidence: The roof is a broad domed slope with a lighter ridge and tile columns. It overhangs, with a light lower rim at rows 14-15 and a dark eave band at rows 16-17 above the set-back posts and basin. That matches the stall roof and well roof references. The basin has a light rim of about 2 rows and the water panel is flat, but the roof, which is the main volume, shows a clear top slope above a front structure. This is acceptable as 3/4.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 steps (light ridge, light gray, mid blue-gray, dark, deep navy) and some per-tile variation, which is close to the reference roof. The lower half is much flatter. The basin front is a large block of one flat gray (about 14x6 px) with almost no grain. The water panel is a flat blue field with a single highlight bar. The posts are only 3 orange tones with little grain. The outline is dark navy and brown, mostly tinted, but the basin has near-neutral dark edges. Tiles in the lower half carry only about 3-4 colours, so the piece is thinner than the reference well and stall.
